title: OneCoin lies Part 2 - OneCoin lies to muslims about Shariah compliancy and certificate
description: AlHuda CIBE press release where it withdraws its Shariah certificate for Coin Safe: http://alhudacibe.com/pressrelease75.php.

asr.full_text: 1. In the beginning of 2016, OneCoin introduced coin safe option where members can store their coins for 12,18 or 24 month period. The company promises the coin safe users 10,11 or 12% interest correspondingly. In August 2016, 2016 one coin introduced an option for coin safe to circumvent the interest option which is forbidden in Sharia law members could now choose what the company calls Sharia compliant option in coin safe which means the members get gift coins instead of yearly interest on October 26 2016 al- Al-Huda, Center of Islamic Banking and Economics, issued Sharia certificate for the CoinSafe product, clearly indicating that the ceridificate is for the CoinSafe product alone, however, OneCoin soon after this released a press release where it lied that OneCoin itself had been declared Sharia compliant. On 28 November, 2016, the Sharia certificate issuer Alhudha, posted a press release on its site, stating that it withdraws the Sharia certificate, due to OneCoin violating the terms of certification, and non-compliance of the guidelines. however, this has not stopped the company, its ambassadors Kary Walra and OneCoin leaders like Tom McMarine to falsely claim that OneCoin is Sharia compliant and Sharia certified, thus not only lying but specifically lying to 1.8 billion Muslims. We do not work on on standards We are transparent Everything doctor Ruja ever said Has come true Even better than that One life is also Sharia certified and compliant One Life Company Ambassador Kare Wangwus and OneCoin leaders like Tom McMurrin are blatantly lying, especially to 1.8 billion Muslims. Neither One Life nor OneCoin have never been Sharia-compliant or had a Sharia certificate. Only the coinsafe product had a Sharia certificate for about a month, until the certificate was revoked by the issuer, Alhuda, due to One Life Company lies and violations of the certificate terms. The company and its representatives continue to deceive Muslims in order to promote the fraudulent activities of OneCoin.

textual.context: The ASR presents these statements while discussing and criticizing OneCoin's CoinSafe product; it is unclear from these records whether the offer was promotional material, commentary, or both.
textual.potential_relevance: A promised financial return or gift-coin benefit is linked to storing coins for a specified period and choosing a particular product option, which may require assessment of the offer's terms and representation.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish whether members paid, transferred assets, received the stated returns, or experienced a loss.

textual.observation: The source describes a Sharia certificate issued for the CoinSafe product alone, followed by a claimed broader representation that OneCoin itself was Sharia compliant, and later reports that the issuer withdrew the certificate.

textual.context: The broader-compliance statement and the characterization of it as a lie are presented by the ASR speaker. The description separately identifies a press release about withdrawal of the CoinSafe certificate.
textual.potential_relevance: The records describe a claimed endorsement whose stated scope was limited to one product but was reportedly represented as applying to the wider company, followed by reported withdrawal of that certificate.
textual.limitations: The records do not independently verify the referenced press release, the certificate's original wording, or whether the broader claim was officially made beyond the ASR's account.

textual.observation: The ASR reports that company representatives continued to claim that OneCoin and One Life were Sharia compliant or Sharia certified after the certificate was reportedly revoked.

textual.context: These are allegations and quoted claims reported by the ASR speaker in a critical video; the records do not establish whether the named representatives made the claims outside the speaker's account.
textual.potential_relevance: A claimed religious certification or compliance status is linked to company and product promotion despite the source's account of a limited and later revoked certificate.
textual.limitations: The records do not provide the representatives' original statements, the exact revocation notice, or independent confirmation of the claimed affiliations.

visual.observation: A OneLife web interface displays a "CREATE NEW COINSAFE ACCOUNT" form with selectable "Coinsafe: profit sharing ratio" options, including percentages and time periods, plus a transaction-password field and a "Send" button.
visual.context: The frames show an account-creation interface and an accompanying presentation about OneCoin; whether this is promotion, demonstration, or reporting is unclear from the sampled frames.
visual.potential_relevance: The interface links selecting a stated profit-sharing return and entering a transaction password to submitting a new account request, which is a task-relevant reward-and-action relationship.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish whether an account was successfully created, whether any payment or transfer occurred, or whether the displayed returns were delivered.

visual.observation: A displayed certificate states that procedures were compliant with Shariah and identifies an "ONECOIN-SAVING PRODUCT (COIN SAFE)," while a later press-release page visibly states that the institution did not certify OneCoin as Shariah compliant and that the certificate was withdrawn.
visual.context: The material is presented as a clarification or warning about the relationship between the certificate, OneCoin, and the Coinsafe product.
visual.potential_relevance: The visible certificate presents an institutional compliance or endorsement association for the product, while the later clarification visibly disclaims that certification and describes its withdrawal; this conflicting endorsement presentation conditionally merits review.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames do not independently verify the document, the issuing institution, the web pages, or the chronology beyond the text shown.

textual_context_notes.observation: The title and ASR frame the material as criticism of alleged false Sharia-compliance claims and reference a certificate withdrawal.

The video includes black title cards asserting that OneLife, an ambassador, and OneCoin leaders were lying, and that the certificate was revoked because of alleged company lies and violations of certificate terms.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it reports and criticizes OneCoin and OneLife claims about Shariah compliance rather than promoting them. It explains that the certificate applied only to the CoinSafe product and was later withdrawn, without asking viewers to invest, provide data, or send money.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The central activity is examining and criticizing an alleged discrepancy between a Coin Safe product certificate and a broader OneCoin compliance claim. The depicted Coin Safe offer is third-party subject matter, not a solicitation by the video.
